paper_title: Searching for Time-Dependent Axion Dark Matter Signals in Pulsars
notes: Paper reports a new measured exclusion limit on axion-photon coupling using time-domain matched-filter analysis of PSR J2144−3933 radio observations from MeerKAT. The limit g_agamma < 5.5 × 10^-11 GeV^-1 is valid over the mass range m_a = 3.9–4.7 μeV (corresponding to observing frequency ~1.0 GHz). This is encoded as a horizontal line (mass-independent bound over the stated range). The paper uses a fiducial pulsar distance D = 0.165 kpc (parallax measurement); an alternative distance D = 0.29 kpc from electron density models yields a weaker limit of 9.6 × 10^-11 GeV^-1. The DM density assumed is ρ_DM ≈ 0.45 GeV/cm^3 (standard NFW profile extrapolation for the Galactic halo). The limit is a 2σ (≈95% CL) upper bound derived from matched-filter SNR analysis. The paper emphasizes the advantage of time-domain over frequency-domain searches for signals with significant time variation due to pulsar magnetosphere rotation. | selector: text over figure_vision (quality (1, 1, 1, 1, 1, 0, 0.92, 2))
